headline: Tech Strength Meets Geopolitical Fog as Friday Open Approaches
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Friday as traders digest a largely constructive Thursday session — one in which 344 of 545 names in our universe advanced — against a backdrop of escalating Middle East tension. Oil prices are in focus after rallying over the course of the week as U.S.-Iran hostilities resumed, with diesel reaching a record high and Gulf shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz running below its 10-day average. Vice President Vance declined Thursday to characterize the conflict as a war or offer any timeline for resolution, leaving investors without a clear geopolitical anchor heading into the weekend.

Thursday's session was led by software, which gained 1.58% as a group, followed by industrials up 1.03% and homebuilders adding 0.59%. Semiconductors and consumer names edged fractionally higher, while healthcare slipped 0.14% and the energy and materials sectors each retreated — down 0.57% and 0.60% respectively — despite the broader crude tailwind. The day's standout mover was Snowflake, which surged 16.55% to pace all gainers, while Victoria's Secret dropped 13.17% to lead decliners.

At Friday's open, watch crude and diesel benchmarks closely alongside any fresh headlines out of the Hormuz corridor. South Korea has disclosed it is reviewing military options related to the strait, adding another variable to an already complex supply picture. With no major domestic data releases scheduled before the bell, sentiment is likely to take its cues from energy pricing and any overnight geopolitical developments.

briefs.headline: Snowflake Rockets Higher, Anchors Software Rally
briefs.body: Snowflake surged 16.55% on Thursday, making it the day's top performer across the full universe and helping lift the software sector 1.58% — the best of any group. Twilio and CrowdStrike also contributed meaningfully, rising 6.06% and 5.68% respectively, signaling broad-based appetite for enterprise technology names.

briefs.headline: Diesel at Record High as Hormuz Traffic Slows
briefs.body: U.S. diesel prices hit a record high as simultaneous pressures — renewed U.S.-Iran fighting and constrained Gulf shipping — tightened the supply outlook. Gulf tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continued to run below its 10-day average, according to data cited by Reuters, keeping the energy complex on edge ahead of the weekend.

briefs.headline: Vance Pushes Back on 'War' Label, Offers No End Date
briefs.body: Vice President Vance told reporters Thursday that the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict should not be characterized as a war, while stopping short of providing any timeline for its conclusion. Separately, U.S. officials confirmed a probe into an airstrike that Iran says struck a wedding party, with independent analysis suggesting a direct hit by a U.S. munition.

briefs.headline: Victoria's Secret Leads Consumer Decliners with Sharp Drop
briefs.body: Shares of Victoria's Secret fell 13.17% on Thursday, the steepest single-session decline in the universe. The move dragged on the broader consumer sector, which managed only a narrow 0.17% advance for the day, suggesting the selling was largely company-specific rather than a sector-wide rotation.

briefs.headline: Seoul Weighs Hormuz Options as Regional Stakes Rise
briefs.body: South Korea's government disclosed it is actively reviewing military contingency options related to the Strait of Hormuz, though no decision has been reached, according to an official cited by Reuters. The disclosure underscores how the U.S.-Iran confrontation is beginning to draw in regional powers with significant shipping and energy exposure.

briefs.headline: Billionaire Wealth Climbs to $15.1 Trillion, Fueling Private Security Demand
briefs.body: A new report pegged total billionaire wealth at $15.1 trillion last year, a figure that analysts say is helping drive a parallel boom in personal protection services. The private security industry has grown into a $50 billion market, according to separate industry data, with ultra-high-net-worth demand cited as a primary growth engine.
